note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute onset left-sided headache since this morning; woke around 5:30 am with severe head pain.
  - No known clear trigger; patient under work-related stress; history of anxiety.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Headache persisting since onset; previously had headaches but not this severe.
  - Light sensitivity noted; dizziness initial but resolved; no fever.
- ENT-related symptoms:
  - Photophobia (sensitivity to bright lights); no neck stiffness; no reported throat, nasal, ear symptoms.
- Past episodes and treatments:
  - History of headaches; no migraine history confirmed.
  - On sertraline for anxiety/depression (current medication).
  - Took paracetamol this morning with little relief.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: none known.
  - Current meds: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) taken this morning.
  - Other meds: None.
- Social context:
  - Lives with partner; non-smoker; cat at home; exercises (running ~3x/week).

Objective:
- Observable findings: Not examined; no documented exam findings.
- Airway/breathing: Not described.
- Mental status: Not described.
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Additional: Not stated whether a companion/support person was present.

Assessment:
- Primary clinical impression:
  - Headache with features compatible with tension-type headache or migraine in the context of stress/anxiety.
  - Left-sided predominance with photophobia supports migraine consideration; stress/workload may contribute.
- Red flags: Not reported (no fever, neck stiffness, focal neuro symptoms, or signs of systemic infection).

Plan:
- Medications and home management:
  - Ibuprofen: first-line consideration for migraine-type headache; dose/route/frequency not documented. Paracetamol to continue as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Hydration and sleep: aim for 7–8 hours sleep per night; 1.5–2 liters of fluids per day (excluding caffeine).
- Non-pharmacologic and lifestyle measures:
  - Consider taking time off work (self-certify for one week) to reduce stress.
  - Explore counselling options; provided link for local counselling self-referral.
- Follow-up and escalation:
  - Follow-up appointment scheduled for one week.
  - If not improving, consider blood tests or other evaluations as needed.
  - If symptoms worsen or new red flags arise, contact the clinic promptly for reassessment.
  - Note: Summary of plan and danger-sign resource will be provided in notes.
- Additional notes provided to patient:
  - Danger-signs link for headaches to review in own time.
